title: Sine space / walk the equation
question: What is it to stand on sin(x) * cos(z)?
reference: A smooth sin * cos ground with trimesh collision; ridges and troughs invite directional walking. (The wavefunctions sine_space is the room version; this is the floor.)
physical_model: Static ground. Height is wave_amplitude * sin(x f + px) * cos(z f + pz) * height_scale.

slot.note: Fitted by TopologySpace.fit_slot: fills the slot; a flat RIM rim_width wide lies at the meeting level (the pool floor, or the wall plane) all round, so the piece drops into a basin or a wall frame flush with its edge; the relief rises inward of the rim across edge_band; the lowest point rests on the floor and the highest stays 0.1 m under the rim height. Also stands alone with no slot.

parameters.label: Relief
parameters.question: The overall rise; in a slot the pool depth caps it.

parameters.label: Phase X
parameters.question: Where does the first ridge stand?

parameters.label: Edge band
parameters.question: How far inward of the rim does the relief take to rise?

parameters.label: Flat rim
parameters.question: How wide is the flat band at the edge that meets the basin or the frame?

parameters.label: Bump map
parameters.question: Shade the relief as a normal map, so the walked mesh may be coarser than the look?

parameters.label: Collision step
parameters.question: The trimesh from every n-th vertex: 2 is a quarter of the triangles, 4 a sixteenth.
